newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Popular plans further Greek expansion.
newsitem.headline: Popular plans further Greek expansion.

text.p: The European Popular Bank, the Greek subsidiary of the Cyprus Popular Bank plans to branch out into leasing, factoring and mutual funds by the end of 1997, the bank said on Thursday.

The bank, established in Greece in 1992, posted profits before depreciation, provisions for bad debts and taxes, of 1.4 billion drachmas ($5.1 million) in 1996, a rise of 28 percent from gains the year before.
A company news release issued in Nicosia said total assets rose by 69 percent to 130 billion drachmas, while loans and advances more than doubled to 37 billion drachmas in 1996.
This year the bank will open four new branches, bringing its total network to nine, and will launch factoring, leasing and mutual funds services, the news release said.

"Our long term goal is the firm establishment of the European Popular Bank in Greece as an ecumenical bank with prospects of expanding to the wider European region," the chairman of the board of directors Kikis Lazarides was quoted as saying.
The Cyprus Popular Bank, the second largest commercial bank in Cyprus, owns 60 percent of the European Popular Bank.
HSBC Holdings PLC holds a 22 percent stake in Cyprus Popular Bank.
